An ancient crypt of carved stone sarcophagi receding into darkness, dust thick on the lids, cobwebbed pillars rising into shadow, a low arched ceiling pressing close overhead.
A vast natural cavern bristling with stalactites, a black underground lake reflecting faint torchlight, the far walls lost entirely in impenetrable dark.
A ruined dwarven vault of colossal carved pillars and broken stone, gold-veined walls catching flickering light, the great hall swallowed by shadow beyond the reach of flame.
A flooded sewer-tunnel knee-deep in black water, mossy brickwork arching low overhead, rats skittering across submerged ledges, the passage bending away into absolute darkness ahead.
A sunken temple half-drowned in still black water, carved serpent columns rising from the flood, cracked altar stones barely visible beneath the surface, the vaulted ceiling lost in gloom.
A torch-lit catacomb of bone-lined walls, skulls stacked in neat rows receding endlessly, the narrow passage tightening as it descends, shadows pooling thick between each yellowed niche.
A collapsed mine-shaft choked with splintered timber and rubble, a narrow passage forcing itself through the debris, the darkness beyond absolute, the air stale and heavy with old dust.
A forgotten throne-room deep underground, a cracked basalt seat looming on a raised dais, tattered banners rotting from iron rings, shadow claiming every corner of the vast cold space.
A pillared hall swallowed by dark, enormous stone columns vanishing upward into a ceiling unseen, the floor worn smooth by countless feet long dead, silence pressing in from all sides.
A spider-webbed tunnel network of low earthen passages, thick silk sheeting every surface, dry husks of creatures hanging in rows, the branching tunnels fading fast into smothering black.
A lava-lit volcanic chamber, rivers of molten rock carving channels through the obsidian floor, the walls glowing orange-red, vast columns of cooled lava rising into a smoke-blackened vault above.
A frozen ice-cave dungeon of blue-white walls translucent as glass, shapes of ancient things suspended deep within the ice, breath misting, the passage narrowing toward total crystalline dark.
A vault of carved demonic faces covering every surface, grinning mouths and hollow stone eyes converging on a central pit, the carved walls descending into depths the torchlight cannot reach.
A fungal grotto where enormous pale mushrooms crowd the floor, faint bioluminescent spores drifting upward through the dark, the cavern ceiling dripping, the far reaches swallowed in dim blue shadow.
A charnel pit-room of tumbled bones piled to the waist, iron chains hanging from the ceiling, rusted cages still occupied, the stench thick and the darkness beyond the pit absolute.
A subterranean library of rotted shelves, crumbling tomes falling to dust at a touch, stone reading desks overturned, the chamber stretching back row after silent row into consuming dark.
A ceremonial sacrificial hall of black marble, a long stone table at its centre stained dark, channelled grooves running to a central drain, the far altar entirely lost in shadow.

A damp alchemical laboratory carved into rock, shattered retorts and cracked stone vessels lining the shelves, strange residue coating the floor, the back wall receding into stained and dripping dark.

A narrow guard-post passage of thick iron portcullises, murder-holes gaping in the ceiling above, torches long cold in their rusted brackets, the corridor pressing tight before dropping into blind dark.
A serpentine river-cavern where black water rushes fast along a stone channel, slick ledges barely wide enough to walk, the rushing sound echoing back from walls unseen in the dark.

A grand underground mausoleum of towering stone effigies, noble figures frozen in silent procession, the carved faces worn blank by damp, the procession disappearing into the chamber's far shadowed end.
A pit-trap gallery of checkered flagstones, several already fallen away into black drops below, the opposite archway barely visible across the gaps, silence rising cold from the unseen floor beneath.
A desecrated chapel hewn from bedrock, a broken stone altar overturned before a carved void symbol, the pews reduced to splinters, the apse behind swallowed entirely in pooled and perfect shadow.
A pressurised steam-vent passage of scalded stone, jets of hot vapour screaming from cracks in the walls, the floor slick and treacherous, the far end a white-blind wall of mist.

A vast underground ossuary of stacked skulls forming walls and vaulted arches, candle niches long extinguished, the ceiling a mosaic of interlocked bones, the central corridor receding deep into bone-white dark.
